# PlayGuard

> A proxy MCP: one MCP server in your client config that runs several MCP servers under the hood — Playwright MCP (bundled, always on), Figma (Framelink `figma-developer-mcp` or Figma's official desktop server), Chrome DevTools MCP, Shopify Dev MCP and Context7 — exposes all their tools through a single connection, and optimizes their responses on the way back.

PlayGuard is free and MIT licensed, runs locally over stdio, requires Node.js 20.18.1+, and is installed by adding one entry to an MCP client config. Which upstreams run is decided by environment variables in that entry; an upstream without its variable is never started. It works with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, and any other MCP-compatible client.

Install (every upstream on; remove a variable to drop that upstream):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "playguard": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "playguard@latest"],
      "env": {
        "PLAYGUARD_SCREENSHOTS": "redirect",
        "FIGMA_MCP_CMD": "npx",
        "FIGMA_MCP_ARGS": "-y figma-developer-mcp --stdio",
        "FIGMA_API_KEY": "your-figma-api-key",
        "DEVTOOLS_MCP_CMD": "npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest",
        "DEVTOOLS_MCP_ARGS": "--headless --isolated",
        "SHOPIFY_DEV_MCP_CMD": "npx -y @shopify/dev-mcp@latest",
        "CONTEXT7_MCP_CMD": "npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp@latest"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Who it's for: developers whose agents do front-end work — browser QA, Figma-to-code, Shopify themes. A typical setup runs Figma MCP and Playwright MCP together in one entry: the agent reads the design, builds it, then checks the live page against the Figma node with `playguard_compare_design`. Cursor reads the same JSON from `.cursor/mcp.json`; Codex takes the same command, args and env as TOML in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.playguard]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "playguard@latest"]

[mcp_servers.playguard.env]
PLAYGUARD_SCREENSHOTS = "redirect"
```

## What it does

- **One connection, several upstreams** — tool lists are merged and each call is routed to the upstream that advertised the tool. Optional upstreams start lazily and are isolated: a failing one only removes its own tools.
- **Session recovery** — dead-session errors (`Target.*closed`, `Browser.*closed`, `connect ECONNREFUSED`, `crashed`) are intercepted; Playwright MCP is restarted, the last URL restored, the call retried. Crashed DevTools / Shopify Dev / Context7 processes are respawned too.
- **Snapshot compaction** — only lines carrying a `[ref=]` handle plus structural landmarks are kept, typically removing 70-90% of an accessibility tree. Delta snapshots, `UNCHANGED` repeats, eval cache, optional prefetch.
- **Figma** — Framelink responses run through eight optimizer modules with structural budget trimming (re-fetchable stubs, nothing dropped silently). The official desktop server (`FIGMA_MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp`, no API key, paid Dev/Full seat) is passed through whole. Figma's remote server `mcp.figma.com` cannot be proxied.
- **Chrome DevTools MCP** — long network lists become summaries (Shopify store 34K → ~1K chars), noisy headers and HTML bodies are trimmed, snapshots are compacted with `UNCHANGED`/delta; usage statistics and CrUX are off by default. It drives its own Chrome, separate from `browser_*`.
- **Shopify Dev and Context7** — doc answers rewritten to compact markdown, duplicate chunks dropped, tool lists compacted (Context7 5.9K → 2.6K chars), lookups cached on disk for 24 h, identical repeats answered with a one-line `UNCHANGED`.
- **Accessibility audit** — `playguard_a11y_audit` runs axe-core in the current page and returns WCAG 2.0–2.2 A/AA violations grouped by rule.
- **Design diff** — `playguard_compare_design` compares a Figma node against the live DOM element implementing it and reports per-property mismatches numerically (Framelink).
- **Screenshot policy** — `allow`, `warn` (default), `block`, or `redirect` (screenshot replaced by a snapshot, `{visual:true}` as the escape hatch).
- **Privacy** — Chrome DevTools, Shopify Dev and Context7 each get a filtered environment (`FIGMA_API_KEY` never reaches them, `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` reaches Context7 only); keys never reach logs or caches. `raw: true` on a call returns the untouched upstream response.
- **Analytics** — every call is logged as NDJSON; `npm run analyze` reports tokens saved per upstream, cache hits, and per-tool latency.

## Links

- [Overview](https://playguard.dev/): what PlayGuard is, with before/after numbers and an interactive config builder.
- [How PlayGuard works](https://playguard.dev/docs/): full technical walkthrough — upstreams, routing, compaction, session recovery, Figma (Framelink and official), Chrome DevTools, Shopify Dev and Context7, accessibility audit, design diff, and every environment variable.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/ZenyaDAR/PlayGuard): MIT licensed, tests run in CI on every push.
- [Package on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/playguard): `npx -y playguard@latest`.
